clues: An outer epithelial layer developed from surface ectoderm.
It lacks direct blood vessels and relies on diffusion from below.
It is the outermost layer of the skin overlying the dermis.
A connective tissue layer situated deep to the surface epithelium.
It contains collagen and elastic fibers that confer strength and resilience.
It lies directly beneath the epidermis and contains hair follicles and glands.
Linear patterns mapped across the surface of the body.
They reflect the main orientation of fibrous bundles in deeper skin.
Surgeons often follow these cleavage lines for better cosmetic scarring.
An exocrine gland of the skin that produces an oily lipid mixture.
Its secretion helps lubricate and waterproof hair and skin.
It typically empties sebum into a hair follicle.
A tiny smooth muscle bundle associated with a skin appendage.
Sympathetic stimulation makes it contract during cold or fear.
Its contraction pulls a hair follicle upright to cause gooseflesh.
A coiled tubular gland widely distributed over general body skin.
It releases watery fluid that cools the body through evaporation.
It is a sweat gland that opens directly onto the skin surface.
A connective tissue layer lying between the skin proper and deeper investing tissue.
It commonly contains fat lobules, superficial veins, and cutaneous nerves.
Also called subcutaneous tissue, it sits beneath the dermis.
A deeper membranous layer found in a specific part of the trunk wall.
It attaches below the inguinal ligament to the deep fascia of the thigh.
It is the membranous layer of the lower anterior abdominal superficial fascia.
A layer of connective tissue over the lower front of the trunk.
It is rich in fat and lies superficial to a membranous fascial layer.
It is the superficial fatty layer of the lower anterior abdominal wall.
A tough, organized fibrous layer lying deep to subcutaneous tissue.
It invests muscles and forms compartments, septa, and retinacula.
It is the dense collagenous sheet surrounding limb muscles.
A fibrous partition extending inward from an investing fascial sheath.
It often attaches to bone and increases surface area for muscle origin.
It divides a limb into distinct muscle compartments.
A localized band-like thickening of fibrous tissue near a joint.
It acts like a strap or pulley to prevent tendons from bowstringing.
Thickened deep fascia around the wrist or ankle forms this structure.

terms.sub: Vessels and nerves of skin and fascia
clues: A blood vessel that pierces a fibrous fascial barrier in a limb.
Its valves typically direct blood inward toward deeper vessels.
It connects superficial veins in subcutaneous tissue with deep veins.
A concept in segmental neurology tied to spinal nerves.
It maps a specific band or patch of body surface.
It is the area of skin supplied by sensory fibers of one spinal nerve root.
